title: Aspirin for Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease in Adults
snippet: Aspirin has been shown to reduce the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults over 50 years of age, with a relative risk reduction of approximately 15% in several meta-analyses. The number needed to treat is approximately 67 over 2 years.

title: Cardiovascular Efficacy and Safety Profile of Low-Dose Aspirin
snippet: Long-term low-dose aspirin therapy (75-100 mg daily) demonstrates efficacy in secondary prevention of cardiovascular events. Safety concerns include increased bleeding risk, which must be weighed against the cardiovascular benefit in individual patient populations.

title: Metformin in Prevention of Type 2 Diabetes: A Landmark Study
snippet: The Diabetes Prevention Program demonstrated that metformin reduces the progression from impaired glucose tolerance to type 2 diabetes by 31% in overweight adults. The effect was particularly strong in adults under 60 years of age.
